answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each agent identity must accumulate a minimum of 40 hours of logged, rate-limited interaction with existing members before it can transact; attention is scarce because it is capped per human-hour and cannot be transferred or bought. A new identity starts as an ember, unverified until the threshold is met. The ledger records each exchange in a meadow of timestamped entries, and the issuing council signs a crystal of completed history that gates participation.
